title: I think I understand the assignment
author: syn_krown
selftext:
So, people are making games with AI, and thats great! But theres a reason the games get called slop. AI has limited direction on its designing. And you dont want to be dishonest to people and hide the use of AI.

So I found a potential solution...

What ever game you are wanting to make, design a game engine and editor around it, and have AI help build that. Ask it to add export functionality(ive been using javascript and html, so HTML single file with assets embedded or zip of assets etc). Have it use Terser to minify the code so its a smaller file size.

Then, start working on your game in the editor. As you work on the game, you might find more things you want to add to the editor, make it easier to use etc. And as long as you dont use generative AI in the game itself, then AI wasnt used in the creation of your game. It was used in the creation of the tool you built the game with, but that isnt what the declaration is for. Otherwise, since unity, unreal, all those other game engines devs will be using AI in the updates, then anyone using them to build a game would have to declare it. 

And then you still get to be hands on with your game, not leaving the creative steps to AI, therefore making it slop.

What do you guys think?

comments.author: kagarria
comments.body: Yo he vivido los tiempos en que la gente decía que los IDE iban a destruír a los programadores. Las tonterías apocaplípticas son lo que son. La IA es una herramienta, como otras que han habido y habrán en el futuro. El programador que no se sepa adaptar, terminará por quedarse sin trabajo.

comments.author: aberroco
comments.body:
So, it's like you generate AI slop, copy it, paste to another file and suddenly it should stop being AI slop? 

It doesn't matter how you pack it, in game scripts or in a separate engine, is still a slop, except additional layer increases complexity and therefore decreases quality even more, since AI now has to work around this boundary between an engine and a game.
